easy.def: Work that a person does to earn money.
examples: Dad has a new job.
She likes her job.
A baker has a job.

more.def: The work that a person does regularly to earn money.
examples: My aunt has a job at the post office.
A firefighter has an important job in our town.
He is looking for a job after school.

easy.def: A task you have to do.
examples: Feeding the fish is my job.
It was a big job.
She did a good job.

more.def: A task or duty that someone has to do.
examples: Setting the table is my job on school nights.
Cleaning the garage was a big job.
You did a great job on your science poster.
The jockey rode the horse.
A jockey is small.
The jockey wore bright colors.

more.def: A person whose job is to ride horses in races.
examples: The jockey leaned low over the horse.
The jockey wore a bright cap and silks.
A small jockey won the race.
A jocular man.
The jocular coach.
He was jocular.

more.def: Fond of joking; humorous and playful.
examples: The jocular coach cracked jokes.
He was a jocular man who always smiled.
She gave a jocular reply.
She wore jodhpurs.
The jodhpurs are tan.
Jodhpurs are for riding.

more.def: Pants for horse riding that fit tightly from the knee to the ankle.
examples: She wore jodhpurs and boots to ride.
The rider tucked her jodhpurs into tall boots.
Jodhpurs let you move easily on a horse.
A joey is a baby kangaroo.
The joey is in the pouch.
The joey hops.

more.def: A baby kangaroo, wallaby or other animal with a pouch.
examples: The joey peeked out of its mother's pouch.
A joey drinks its mother's milk.
The little joey hopped after its mother.
Dad jogs each morning.
I jogged around the park.
We jog to school.

more.def: To run at a slow, steady speed, usually as exercise.
examples: My dad jogs around the park every morning before work.
We jogged slowly to the corner and then walked the rest of the way.
The coach asked us to jog two laps around the field.
We went for a jog.
A morning jog is fun.
She took a jog by the lake.

more.def: A slow, steady run for exercise.
examples: We went for a jog along the river after school.
A short jog warms up your muscles before a game.
He takes a jog around the block every morning.

easy.def: A person who runs slowly for exercise.
examples: A jogger ran by.
The jogger wore sneakers.
A jogger passed the park.

more.def: A person who runs at a slow, steady pace for exercise.
examples: A jogger ran past us on the path.
The jogger wore bright shoes.
Many joggers use the trail in the morning.
Join the two pieces.
The bridge joins two towns.
Join hands in a circle.

more.def: To connect or fasten things together.
examples: A bridge joins the two sides of the river.
Join the two ropes with a knot.
The two streams join to make one river.

easy.def: To become part of a group.
examples: Join our team.
She joined the club.
Can I join you?

more.def: To become a member of a group, or to do something together with others.
examples: She joined the choir last fall.
Can I join you for lunch?
Several new players joined the team.

easy.def: A place where two bones meet.
examples: My knee is a joint.
Joints let you bend.
The elbow is a joint.

more.def: A place in the body where two bones meet and can move.
examples: Your knee is a joint.
Joints let your arms and legs bend.
The doctor checked her elbow joint.

easy.def: A place where two things are joined.
examples: The joint in the pipe.
The wood joint is tight.
A joint in the table.

more.def: A place where two parts are joined together.
examples: Glue held the joint of the chair.
The plumber fixed a leaking joint in the pipe.
The two boards meet at a tight joint.
They own it jointly.
They did it jointly.
The prize was won jointly.

more.def: In a way that is shared by two or more people.
examples: The twins own the toy jointly.
They wrote the book jointly.
The prize was won jointly by two teams.

easy.def: A beam that holds up a floor.
examples: The joist holds the floor.
A joist is wood.
The joist is strong.

more.def: One of the long beams that support a floor or ceiling.
examples: Wooden joists held up the floor.
The carpenter nailed boards across the joists.
The ceiling joists were thick and strong.

easy.def: Something funny you say to make people laugh.
examples: Tell us a joke.
Her joke was funny.
I know a joke about a cow.

more.def: A funny story or saying that makes people laugh.
examples: My dad tells a joke at every dinner.
The clown's joke made the whole class laugh.
She told a joke about a talking banana.
I was only joking.
He jokes with us.
They joked at lunch.

more.def: To say something funny or not serious, to make people laugh.
examples: Dad joked that the dog was reading the paper.
She was only joking when she said she would eat the whole cake.
The friends joked and laughed all through lunch.
My dad is a joker.
The joker made us laugh.
He is a class joker.

more.def: A person who likes to tell jokes and play tricks.
examples: My dad is a joker who loves puns.
The class joker made us all laugh.
The joker wore a funny hat.

easy.def: A playing card with a picture of a clown.
examples: I got the joker.
The joker is in the deck.
The joker is a card.

more.def: A card in a deck with a picture of a jester, used in some games.
examples: I drew the joker from the deck.
The joker is a wild card.
The deck has two jokers.
He is a jokester.
The jokester laughed.
A jokester tells funny jokes.

more.def: A person who likes to tell jokes and play pranks.
examples: He is the class jokester.
The jokester made everyone laugh.
The jokester hid a toy spider in the lunch box.

easy.def: In a funny way, not seriously.
examples: She said it jokingly.
He jokingly said no.
They jokingly argued.

more.def: In a way that is meant as a joke.
examples: She jokingly called him a tall tree.
He jokingly said he would eat the whole cake.
They jokingly argued about who was faster.
The room was full of jollity.
There was jollity.
Jollity filled the hall.

more.def: Fun and laughter.
examples: The party was full of jollity.
There was great jollity at the feast.
Laughter and jollity filled the hall.
The jolly man laughed a lot.
The jolly baker sang as he worked.
We sang a jolly song.

more.def: Cheerful, friendly, and full of good humor.
examples: Our jolly uncle always tells the funniest jokes.
The jolly crowd sang songs on the bus ride home.
Grandpa was in a jolly mood at the party.
The car gave a jolt.
I felt a jolt.
A jolt shook the bus.

more.def: A sudden, rough shake or bump, or a sudden shock.
examples: The bus gave a jolt as it hit a bump.
The loud noise gave us a jolt.
I felt a jolt when I touched the cold wall.
The bus jolted.
The noise jolted me.
The car jolted.

more.def: To move or shake with a sudden rough movement.
examples: The bus jolted as it went over the bump.
The loud noise jolted me awake.
The truck jolted down the rough road.

easy.def: To push roughly in a crowd.
examples: The crowd jostled.
I was jostled.
The kids jostled for a seat.

more.def: To bump or push against people in a crowd.
examples: The crowd jostled to get a good view.
I was jostled in the busy hall.
The kids jostled one another at the door.
I jot a note.
She jotted a list.
Jot down your name.

more.def: To write something down quickly and briefly.
examples: I jotted a note so I would remember.
She jotted down the phone number.
Jot your idea on a piece of paper.

easy.def: A book where you write what happens each day.
examples: I write in my journal.
The journal is blue.
She keeps a journal.

more.def: A notebook in which you write about your thoughts and what you do each day.
examples: I write in my journal every night.
The explorer kept a journal of his trip.
She read her old journal.

easy.def: The job of reporting the news.
examples: She studies journalism.
Journalism is about news.
He works in journalism.

more.def: The work of collecting, writing and reporting the news for newspapers, magazines and television.
examples: She studies journalism so she can write for a newspaper.
Good journalism tells the facts and is fair.
The school has a journalism club that makes a class newspaper.
The journalist wrote a story.
A journalist asked a question.
The journalist works at a paper.

more.def: A person whose job is to gather and write news for newspapers, TV or the internet.
examples: The journalist wrote a story about the flood.
A journalist asked the mayor a question.
The journalist reported live from the scene.
The journey to Grandma's house takes all day.
The bird's journey is very long.
We packed food for the journey.

more.def: A trip from one place to another, usually a long one.
examples: The explorers began their journey across the frozen land.
The journey by train took two days.
Salmon make a long journey up the river.

easy.def: A worker who has learned a trade.
examples: A journeyman is skilled.
The journeyman built a table.
He is a journeyman.

more.def: A worker who has finished learning a trade and is skilled in it.
examples: The journeyman built a fine table.
A journeyman is no longer a beginner.
The journeyman carpenter built the cabinet.

easy.def: To fight on horses with long poles, as knights did long ago.
examples: The knights joust.
They jousted at the fair.
A knight jousted.

more.def: To have a contest on horseback in which two knights charge at each other with long poles, as they did in the Middle Ages.
examples: Knights jousted on horseback at the royal fair.
At the festival, actors in armor jousted for the crowd.
The two knights jousted to win the prize.
The jovial man laughed.
A jovial host.
The jovial baker.

more.def: Cheerful, friendly and full of fun.
examples: The jovial baker greeted everyone with a smile.
Our jovial host told jokes.
The jovial crowd sang along.

easy.def: The loose skin under the chin or on the cheek.
examples: The dog has big jowls.
Her jowl shook.
A dog's jowls hang.

more.def: The loose, hanging skin on the lower cheek or under the chin.
examples: The bulldog's jowls hung down.
His jowls shook as he laughed.
Dogs with big jowls often drool.
The puppy jumped with joy.
We sang with joy.
The baby's laugh brings me joy.

more.def: A feeling of great happiness.
examples: Her face was full of joy when she saw her grandparents.

Reading is one of the great joys of my life.
A joyful song.
The joyful kids danced.
She was joyful.

more.def: Feeling or showing great happiness.
examples: The joyful children danced around the room.
We sang a joyful song at the party.
She gave a joyful shout when she heard the news.
The children played joyfully.
The dog barked joyfully.
She sang joyfully.

more.def: In a way that shows great happiness.
examples: The children played joyfully in the snow.
The dog barked joyfully when its owner came home.
She sang joyfully on the last day of school.
It was a joyous day.
The joyous song made us clap.
She gave a joyous shout.

more.def: Full of great happiness.
examples: It was a joyous day for the whole family.
Joyous music filled the hall at the party.
The children gave a joyous cheer when school ended.
The children played joyously.
She sang joyously.
The bells rang joyously.

more.def: In a way that shows great joy.
examples: The children ran joyously into the snow.
She sang joyously in the shower.
Church bells rang joyously on the holiday.

easy.def: A stick you move to play a game.
examples: I move the joystick.
The joystick controls the game.
He held the joystick.

more.def: A lever that you move in different directions to control a game, plane or machine.
examples: She moved the joystick to steer the spaceship in the game.
The pilot held the joystick steady.
The joystick controls the robot arm.
